summary.text: Braeden Oswald is the Republican candidate for Utah House of Representatives District 24 in the November 3, 2026 general election, in which he faces Democratic incumbent Grant Amjad Miller.

A retired U.S. Marine Corps and Utah National Guard veteran, he said in a Ballotpedia survey that he wants to bring the parties closer to the middle and focus on housing, health care costs, small business relief, financial literacy and managed growth.

paragraphs.text: Braeden Oswald served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 1994 to 2023.
He earned a high school diploma from Park City High School, an associate degree from Salt Lake Community College in 2008 and a bachelor's degree from Excelsior College in 2017.
In a Ballotpedia survey, Oswald said he is a lifetime Utah resident who has lived in District 24 for more than 13 years.

He said he retired as a Chief Warrant Officer-3 after 28 years of service in the Marine Corps and the Utah National Guard, and has also worked as a corrections officer for the Salt Lake County Sheriff's Office and owned a small business.
Oswald said his campaign platform has five areas: home ownership, affordable health care, small business relief, financial literacy in schools and responsible management of growth.
